name: Computational & Systems Analysis
description: Agent-based modeling, mathematical simulation, machine learning, network analysis, optimization, and statistical inference applied to policy problems. Distinguished by integration with qualitative insights and stakeholder input.

included: Economic and labor supply simulation models
Health system and workforce demand modeling
Cybersecurity games and interdependent network models
LLMs applied to social systems and behavioral simulation
Optimization of policy and intervention strategies
Decision intelligence and reinforcement learning for policy
Causal inference integrated with computational models
excluded: Pure within-host biological models with no policy relevance
Pure theoretical physics without transferability to policy
Pure network science without explicit policy application
Non-policy simulation ecosystems with no intervention layer

interdisciplinarity.preferred: 2–3 tightly coupled disciplines (e.g. math + epidemiology + policy)
interdisciplinarity.avoid: Overly diffuse multi-field consortia without clear computational core
